sourceIndependence: Existing day adjudicator remains canonical runtime owner; P1 is legislation/source research only.
interpretationCaveat: RGMR clauses from 1960 Code are source-referenced; original signed printed-edition/page collation still required. Legal interpretation of §4 versus RG111(a) held.

rules.decision: Resolve liturgical day under 1960 Code, 1962 Missal and applicable particular calendars; modern observance metadata cannot substitute Mass or Office.
Two liturgical days on one date: use table of precedence; lower ranked feast may be commemorated or omitted, not automatically replaced.
Only eligible impeded first-class feast transfers under accidental occurrence; preserves its class.
Separate permanent reassignment with diocesan/institute/local reach from accidental transfer.
Vespers concurrence differs from Mass occurrence; do not use Vespers preference as a Mass switch.
Classes, Sundays, seasonal ferias, vigils and local feasts evaluated by actual date.
September Ember Wednesday, Friday and Saturday are II-class ferias and block ordinary III-class substitution.
Privileged: Sunday, I class, Christmas octave, September Ember, ferias of Advent/Lent/Passiontide, greater Litanies at Mass.
Other commemorations ordinary unless another rubric provides a specific treatment.
Mass or Office of Peter includes Paul and vice versa; inseparable paired prayer is counted as one.
On I-class days only a privileged commemoration may be admitted.
Nonconventual Sung Mass has the same privileged-only commemoration restriction regardless of host day class.
One II-class feast commemoration on II-class Sundays, omitted if a privileged commemoration intervenes.
On other II-class days at most one privileged or ordinary commemoration.
On III/IV-class days at most two commemorations, subject to all other rubrics.
Exclude redundant mysteries/person invocations and conflicting seasonal orations.
Seasonal commemoration first; then table of precedence; omit any excess.
Exact Latin conclusion depends on prayer addressee and mentions of Son/Holy Spirit; do not manufacture formula.
Commemoration at Mass uses Collect, Secret, Postcommunion; own conclusion except expressly under-one-conclusion cases.
Identical-wording substitutions, ritual prayers, votive prayer and oratio imperata have distinct hierarchy; not all are commemorations.
Multiple-lesson Ember Mass orations have special placement; feria commemoration uses specified first oration.
For just cause, festival Mass in wider sense on permitted III-class days and III-class vigils; saint canonized after 26 July 1960 on established universal liturgical date.
Different faculty for votive saint Mass; apply complete votive day/class restrictions, not feast rule.
If missa festiva latiore sensu is celebrated, full proper Office may follow; Office permission is not a Mass choice.
Ordinary commemoration of omitted traditional feast or vigil required; must be reconciled with pre-existing comms and form.
1962 pro aliquibus locis > approved Holy See traditional Supplement > edition-appropriate Common; ad libitum choice only among available forms of that Common.

Optional separate commemoration on III/IV day only if saint/mystery specifically entered for that date in 1962 pro aliquibus locis or approved traditional Supplement; fallback Common does not establish entitlement.
In religious institute/society houses, superior determines use in Conventual Mass or common/choir Office, not the celebrant.
Exact 70 listed III-class feasts cannot be displaced; use canonical resolver identity, not month/day-only lookup.
Protected feasts may be celebrated on III-class Lent or Passiontide feria, commemorating the feria as required.
External solemnity is an authorized distinct Mass circumstance; no automatic Sunday transfer or universal saint permission.
Votive Mass classes/privileges and restrictions require a separate exact rubric evaluation.

rules.decision: Diocese, titular church, order, house, Oratorian and other permissions need original jurisdictional authority and historical effective dates.
Ordinary commemoration explicitly prescribed by new decree versus nonconventual Sung privileged-only rule; must seek competent authoritative interpretation and actual liturgical form.
Later Doctor proclamation changes saint's title/recognition but does not per se rewrite existing 1962 feast/Proper or create second observance.
